Author: Krishan Pahal
Bench: Krishan Pahal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:75432
Court No. - 65
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 7018 of 2025
Applicant :- Sunny
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Ajay Kumar Yadav

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. List has been revised.

2. Learned A.G.A. has informed that notice to the informant has been served on 25.2.2025.
3. Heard Sri Pradeep Kumar Yadav, Advocate holding brief of Sri Ajay Kumar Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4. Applicant seeks bail in P.S.T. No.2340 of 2024, arising out of Case Crime No.36 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and 5(G)/6 POCSO Act, Police Station- Pachokhara, District- Firozabad, during the pendency of trial.
Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114802044/
1 5.

As per prosecution story, the FIR was instituted stating that the applicant had outraged the modesty of the daughter of informant by enticing her away on 9.2.2024 at about 05:30 p.m.
6.
Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
The FIR is delayed by about two days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.

7. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that the FIR does not indicate any offence of rape in it rather the said allegations have been escalated in the statement of victim recorded U/s 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. after legal consultation.
The victim seems to be a consenting party as she had gone with the applicant to a hotel and had not raised any alarm whatsoever.

8. Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that even the fact of going to hotel stands falsified from the statement of Manager of the said hotel who stated that some other lady had come to the hotel alongwith the applicant and not the victim.
The said fact also expressed her consent.

The victim by her looks seems to be major, although she is stated to be 17 years old as per the ossification test report, as such, a leverage of two years may be granted to the applicant on the upper side.
9. It is further argued by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no medical corroboration of the incident.
There is no criminal antecedent of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 19.9.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
10.
Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

11. The Supreme Court in Jaya Mala vs. State of J & K, (1982) 2 SCC 538 and Mohd. Imran Khan vs.
State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), (2011) 10 SCC 192 has opined that the radiologist cannot predict the correct date of birth rather there is a long margin of 1 to 2 years on either side.

sentences.text: 12. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, taking into consideration the delay in institution of FIR and there being no medical corroboration of the incident, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

13. Let the applicant- Sunny, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114802044/
2 under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

entities.text: Sunny vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
14. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

15. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
